points.t: Acne needing a **topical retinoid**, or a patient on **isotretinoin, acitretin or alitretinoin**.
Retinoic-acid receptor binding **normalises keratinisation**, shrinks sebaceous glands (isotretinoin) and slows turnover.
Topicals: alternate nights, **pea-sized**, sunscreen. Oral retinoids: specialist-initiated with the **MHRA PPP** and mood monitoring.
**Pregnancy exposure** (acitretin: avoid pregnancy 3 years after); **mood change**; lipids / LFTs; **tetracycline** → raised ICP.

cause.lead: Nuclear receptors that reset how skin cells mature.
points: Bind **RAR (α, β, γ)** and **RXR** → regulate keratinocyte proliferation and differentiation; RAR-γ dominates in epidermis (adapalene, trifarotene).
Topicals are **comedolytic and anti-comedogenic**, anti-inflammatory (↓ TLR-2, AP-1), and boost penetration of other agents.
**Isotretinoin** acts on **all four acne mechanisms**: profound sebaceous shrinkage and sebum suppression.
**Acitretin** is anti-proliferative but **not immunosuppressive**: useful when infection or cancer risk rules out immunosuppressants.

visuals.caption: Isotretinoin shrinks the sebaceous gland and clears the plugged follicle (left: before; right: on treatment). That is why it acts on every acne mechanism.
visuals.alt: Follicle with large gland and plug beside a follicle with a shrunken gland

points: **Topical**: adapalene 0.1% (± BPO 2.5% or 0.3%/2.5%), tretinoin with clindamycin, trifarotene: acne (first-line, NG198), photoageing.
**Oral isotretinoin**: severe acne. **Oral alitretinoin**: severe chronic hand eczema (NICE TA177).
**Oral acitretin**: severe, pustular or palmoplantar psoriasis; keratinisation disorders; transplant chemoprevention.
Could they become pregnant? Mental health, lipids / liver, any tetracycline?
**≥ 1 highly effective user-independent method** (LARC, sterilisation) or **two complementary** methods, from 1 month before.
Supervised test before, **ideally monthly** during, **1 month after** (acitretin: periodically for 3 years).
Isotretinoin: mood, sexual function, lipids, LFTs. Acitretin: lipids, LFTs. Alitretinoin: lipids, TFTs, headache.

cards.name: Isotretinoin
cards.clue: Dryness, **mood / psychiatric**, sexual dysfunction, lipids, LFTs, myalgia, IIH, night vision.

cards.name: Acitretin
cards.clue: Dryness, hair loss, nail fragility, lipids / LFTs; **no alcohol** (forms etretinate); no blood donation.

manage.lead: Topicals within IP scope; orals are specialist-initiated.

points: **Pea-sized for the whole face**, at night, on dry skin; alternate nights at first.
Moisturiser and daily SPF; expect ‘purging’ 2–4 weeks, benefit 8–12 weeks.
Contraindicated in pregnancy / planning; no formal PPP, but **ask about pregnancy and contraception** and record.
Inadvertent exposure: stop, reassure risk looks very low, advice from **UKTIS**.
Support PPP checks, mood questions, and bloods per specialist plan.
Oral retinoid exposure in pregnancy: urgent specialist / obstetric referral and Yellow Card.

visuals.caption: A pea-sized amount covers the whole face: dot it on, then spread thinly at night on dry skin.
visuals.alt: Pea-sized gel on fingertip and dotted on a face

limits.t: Oral retinoids are highly teratogenic: PPP applies to anyone who could become pregnant.
New low mood or suicidal thoughts on isotretinoin: stop, same-day referral.

items.t: **Low mood, anxiety or suicidal thoughts** on isotretinoin: stop, same-day referral.
Possible **pregnancy** on an oral retinoid: stop, urgent specialist advice.
Headache, visual disturbance, vomiting on retinoid + tetracycline: possible **raised ICP**.

pearls.t: Ask every woman on a topical: ‘Could you be pregnant, or planning to be?’ and document it.
Isotretinoin memory aid: ‘contraception, mood, sex, sun, skin procedures, no tetracyclines’.
Retinoids sensitise to sun: daily SPF.

quiz.q: Why not combine isotretinoin with doxycycline?
How long to avoid pregnancy after acitretin?

quiz.a: At least one highly effective user-independent method, or two complementary user-dependent methods.

quiz.q: How much topical retinoid for the face?
quiz.a: A pea-sized amount for the whole face, at night.
